text: trainer.default_loss uses inputs=batch[:,:-1] and targets=batch[:,1:]. It constructs one-based token positions and includes only lengths[:,0] <= position <= lengths[:,1], multiplies per-token cross-entropy by that mask, and returns the float32 sum divided by ntoks together with ntoks=mask.sum(). This is the literal supplied-boundary rule, not a guarantee that every padded target is excluded: iterate_batches records an L-token sequence with upper length L, so when that row is padded, shifted target position L (original index L, the first padding token) is still included by the inclusive upper comparison. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

AutoContext documents its on-policy distillation objective as reverse KL(student || teacher), so callers must account for this gradient direction instead of assuming the helper directly implements that reverse-KL objective. text: MLX-LM's DWQ path uses teacher logits computed on demand or optionally precomputed top-logit targets, and computes KL between the quantized model's logits and those targets. dwq_quantize explicitly unfreezes scales and biases on affine quantized layers below 8 bits, then optimizes the full model.trainable_parameters() collection; exclusivity to those scales and biases depends on which other parameters were already frozen. This is teacher-guided quantization fine-tuning rather than general student-architecture distillation. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
